plan: Since this is a single-round auction and my value is only $4, I need to be extremely cautious. Bidding too high risks paying more than my value and losing money. Given the possible range of values (0-49), I'll bid slightly above $0 to try and win if others are also risk-averse or have low values. A bid of $0.1 is very low, but could be enough to win against similarly conservative bidders.

Since this is a single-round auction, and I want to maximize profit, I will bid slightly above the expected second-highest bid. Assuming the other bidders also have values between $0 and $49, a reasonable expectation for the second-highest bid is around $11.50 (roughly 1/4 of the maximum possible value). To ensure I win against bids around this level, and to avoid overpaying, I'll bid $22.50. This is just below my value, minimizing risk.

Since this is round 1 of 1, there's no history to learn from. My value is $32. To maximize potential profit, I need to win when my value exceeds the second-highest bid. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning, but not excessively to avoid overpaying. A bid of $32.50 seems reasonable, balancing winning probability and potential cost.
